maya: Heads up — nightly perf on the dedicated INT8 pool shows a ~12% p99 tail increase after the FP8/INT8 calibration run. Repro on stable commit. :eyes:

evan: Oof. Can you paste the repro and a profiler snapshot?

maya: Repro script I used:
```
./tools/bench_infer --model rwd-3b-quant --mode int8 --seq 1024 --batch 1 --kv-prefetch=false
```

perf-bot: Nightly perf summary for job 8841:
p50 8ms  p95 17ms  p99 42ms (prev p99 37ms)
GPU kernel time breakdown:
```
INT8_cutlass_kernel: 28.6ms
FP8_triton_kernel: 9.2ms
KV_cache_miss_handler: 4.1ms
other: 0.1ms
```

sam: Quick hypothesis: arch-prober returned Ampere for one Hopper node under driver 12.3 quirk; CUTLASS tuner then picked a non-split-K kernel path that is slower for our INT8 layout. That would explain a shift in INT8 kernel time.

olivia: Also saw increased KV cache partial-miss rate on that testbed — sequences jump mid-request from 256 -> 1024 due to routing. If the kernel selector treats those as long-seq, different kernel and quant path used.

ev an: Small correction: when KV cache miss rate > ~7% we see fallback to the Triton FP8 path in a few cases because the INT8 kernel penalty combined with extra memcpy makes it worse. Calibration used only short sequences (256), so quant tables might be biased.

maya: Profiler trace (condensed):
```
0.000s: request start
0.012s: kv-lookup hit 72%
0.045s: select_kernel(INT8) -> CUTLASS_variant_B (splitK=false)
0.078s: kernel exec 28.6ms
0.110s: fallback path taken for large tail -> additional triton fp8 run 9.2ms
```

maya: Local experiment: forcing CUTLASS arch to hopper and forcing split-K on brings p99 back below baseline. Numbers:
```
baseline p99 37.0ms
regressed p99 42.0ms
with flags p99 36.5ms
```

sam: Can you share the exact env flags you used? We should avoid hardcoding unless we add a prober fix.

maya: Patch used locally: `CUTLASS_FORCE_ARCH=hopper CUTLASS_FORCE_SPLITK=1 REDWOOD_ENABLE_CUTLASS_TUNER=0 ./tools/bench_infer ...`

sam: OK — plan: 1) add quick guard in arch-prober to prefer hopper codepath for sm >= 70 when driver >= 12.3, 2) emit telemetry when kernel choice mismatches calibration profile, 3) run canary with CUTLASS_FORCE_SPLITK=1 on dedicated-int8 tomorrow.

olivia: I'll dig into the KV cache routing change — routing config changed last week to reduce cold-start latency and might be increasing partial misses. If we can reduce mid-request seq jumps we might avoid the long-seq kernel entirely.

evan: Also: calibration job needs mixed-seq distribution (128/512/1024) not just 256. I'll kick off a calibration-against-mix job to recompute INT8 ranges and see if kernel preference changes.

ci-bot: Started job: https://ci/redwood/jobs/8842 (nightly-calib-mixseq). Will post artifacts to /artifacts/8842 when done.

perf-bot: Uploaded flamegraph: https://perf/redwood/8841/flame.html — INT8_cutlass hot path annotated.

maya: Thanks all. I'll run the canary tomorrow 10:00 PT with CUTLASS_FORCE_SPLITK=1 and the arch-prober guard patch. If canary looks good we'll deploy the prober fix and a short-term runtime flag default to avoid regression. :thumbsup:

sam: Add an alert too: if p99 delta > 5% after calibration jobs, auto-disable CUTLASS_TUNER and mark for manual review.

olivia: noted — I'll open a short PR for the routing tweak and the prober guard.

maya: Great. Follow-ups: evan will post calib artifacts, ci-bot will post canary logs, perf-bot will compare before/after.

evan: I'll also run a micro-benchmark across Ampere/Hopper to ensure no other kernels flip unexpectedly.

maya: Sounds good — thanks everyone.
